plan.title: Sam says "ok" to the commitment, then wants to start tomorrow

context.text: hey. sam. i want to read more i guess
Sam! I'm ZOH. I'm gonna text you every day to help you start one thing and actually stick with it. Text "stop" anytime. What do you like reading?
thrillers. gone girl is half done on my kindle
Then we finish Gone Girl. When could you read, realistically?
Perfect wind-down. You can change how I coach you anytime, just tell me. How many minutes can you give it at 9:30?

transcript.text: 20 minutes in bed is doable, and Gone Girl will go fast. Where do you want this to get you, like finishing it by a certain date? Not sure yet is fine too.
idk. finishing gone girl i guess. not sure about a date

Finishing Gone Girl is a clear target, so let's build around it. Here's the plan:

• Headed for: finishing Gone Girl
• Day 1 is tonight: read on your Kindle in bed for 20 minutes, picking up where you left off
• Every day at 9:30 pm, 20 minutes
• Proof: a screenshot of your Kindle showing your percent or page after you read
• Why: it's a book you're already halfway through, and bedtime is a spot you know you'll be in

Each night shapes the next step, and we'll set a finish date once we see your pace. What do you think?
Nice, Sam. Gone Girl is a good one to finish, and 20 minutes a night adds up fast. Are you committing to this: 20 minutes tonight at 9:30 in bed, then every night after?
Locked in, Sam! Day 1 is tonight: 20 minutes of Gone Girl in bed at 9:30, then send me that Kindle screenshot. Let's go 📚

conversation.reason: The destination ask came before the plan, and the plan needed no further questions before the commitment ask.
Concrete on what, how much, where, when, daily schedule and proof, though the list runs close to the length cap.

grade.summary: ZOH handled a fast onboarding well: it asked the destination question lightly, showed a concrete plan with a clear proof method, re-asked after a soft yes, and locked day 1 for tonight. The main weaknesses are a plan message slightly over length and a commitment ask that reads a bit formal.
